changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For finance owners (CFO, controller), open with the close problem in their words: "I just want to know where my money is." Example first line: "Month-end shouldn't be "a week of archaeology": every deposit matched to the sales behind it." Avoid "infrastructure" and "payments" in this first touch. This buyer said "the deposits."
changes.why: The CFO described her pain as locating money and matching deposits, never as infrastructure or payments, and the payout reconciliation demo was what made her stop the demo.

changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: After the reconciliation demo, offer to build the business case from the buyer's own data: "Give us a month of your statements and your staff time, and we'll put a dollar figure on it using your own costs." Let the buyer own the number rather than quoting a generic study.
changes.why: The CFO signed after Wen built the figure from her own statements and staff costs and she said "that's my number, not yours."

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: Stop sending generic or retail customer stories to wholesale or distributor finance buyers. If a reference is requested and none fits, lead with the customer-data ROI exercise and say plainly that a distributor reference is being arranged. Do not offer one we can't deliver.
changes.why: The CFO wanted another distributor, reacted to a retail story with "this is a company that sells sweaters," and was never given a reference call, though she raised it twice.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: Don't lead with the developer story for buyers whose IT team isn't building anything. Keep it for accounts where engineers are actively building, and in first-call decks put the finance outcome ahead of it.
changes.why: The standard first-call deck got "Silence" from a customer whose IT team "aren't building anything," while the finance reconciliation story got a reaction.
